_meta.status: Transcribed from FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (Allen et al., 1998), pages fetched 14 Oct 2026. Where FAO gives a range, the MIDPOINT is used (noted per crop). Still verify against the source and your local conditions.

sources.kc: FAO-56 Table 12 (single crop coefficients, sub-humid climate, RHmin ~45%, u2 ~2 m/s): https://www.fao.org/4/x0490E/x0490e0b.htm
sources.root_depth_and_p: FAO-56 Table 22 (max effective rooting depth, depletion fraction p for ETc ~5 mm/day): https://www.fao.org/4/x0490E/x0490e0e.htm
sources.soil_water: FAO-56 Example 36: loamy sand thetaFC 0.15 / thetaWP 0.06; silt 0.32 / 0.15; silty clay 0.35 / 0.23 (same chapter as Table 22). Other textures: FAO-56 Table 19.
sources.method: FAO-56 Eq. 82 (TAW), Eq. 83 (RAW), Eq. 85 and 'Forecasting or allocating irrigations' (irrigate when depletion reaches RAW; net depth equals depletion).

rice.note: Kc end is the midpoint of FAO's 0.90-0.60. Paddy rice: p applies to saturation, so no depletion schedule is produced.

wheat.note: FAO 'Spring wheat'. Kc end is the midpoint of 0.25-0.40.

maize.note: FAO 'Maize, field (grain)'. Kc end is the midpoint of 0.60-0.35.

cotton.note: Kc mid is the midpoint of 1.15-1.20; Kc end the midpoint of 0.70-0.50.

mustard.note: PROXY: FAO 'Rapeseed, Canola' (mustard is not listed). Kc mid is the midpoint of 1.0-1.15.

mungbean.note: FAO 'Green Gram and Cowpeas'. Kc end is the midpoint of 0.60 (harvested fresh) and 0.35 (harvested dry).

blackgram.note: PROXY: FAO 'Beans, dry and Pulses' (black gram is not listed separately).
